la:noun:calamitas.html:
călămĭtas, ātis, f.
cf. in columis
.
Lit., loss, injury, damage, mischief, harm: sed ecca ipsa egreditur, nostri fundi calamitas (). Proprie calamitatem rustici grandinem dicunt, Don.; cf. the same on Ter Heaut. 2, 4, 15: robigo genus est vitii, quo culmi pereunt, quod a rusticanis calamitas dicitur, Serv ad : postquam calamitas plures annos arvas calvitur, Pac. ap. ; ; : non ut legatus populi Romani, sed ut quaedam calamitas pervadere videretur, (cf. calamitosus, I A.): in calamitate fructuum,in the failure,, § 227: gregem afficere magnā calamitate,.—
Trop.

călĕo, ui, 2, v. n. (
part. fut. act. călĭtūrus, : caleor = caleo, Caper. ap. P.; prob. only in reference to the impers. caletur, ; ) [etym. dub.; cf. Gr. σκέλλω, σκληρός], to be warm or hot, to glow (object.; opp. frigere, to be cold; while aestuare, to feel, experience warmth; opp. algere, to feel cold; cf. Doed. Syn. III. p. 89).
Lit.: calet aqua; eamus hinc intro ut laves,: sentiri hoc putat, ut calere ignem,: os calet tibi,: sole calente,: terrae alio sole calentes,: calens favilla,: ture calent arae,: calentibus aris,: calituras ignibus aras,: guttae calentes,: epulae,: sulphur,.—Poet. sometimes for aestuare, subject., to feel warm: ut fortunati sunt fabri ferrarii, Qui aput carbones adsident! semper calent,: febre,: rabie,; cf.: caluit et hodie Faustina, Aur. ap. .—
Trop.
To glow in mind, to be roused, warmed, inflamed

(class.; in prose less freq. than ardere): (leones) permixtā caede calentes,inflamed by indiscriminate slaughter,; cf. ; Hirt. ap. : admirando, irridendo calebat,: in re frigidissimā cales, in ferventissimā cales,: animis jam calentibus,: Romani calentes adhuc ab recenti pugnā proelium ineunt,: at ille utendum animis dum spe calerent ratus,are animated,: feminā calere,to become enamored of,; cf.: Lycidan quo calet juventus,: puellā,: amore,; : igne,: desiderio Conjugis abrepti,to be inflamed with desire,; also, to be troubled, perplexed: haec velim explices; etsi te ipsum istic jam calere puto,; Cael. ap. : alio mentis morbo, to labor under (the figure derived from fever, v.supra), ; and so of the passion for scribbling: mutavit mentem populus levis et calet uno Scribendi studio,now the rage for writing and versifying is the general disease of our people,: narratur et prisci Catonis Saepe mero caluisse virtus,; .—

With inf.: tubas audire,; ; .—
With ad: ad nova lucra,—
Of abstract things, to be carried on warmly, to be urged on zealously: illud crimen de nummis caluit re recenti, nunc in causā refrixit,: judicia calent, i. e. magnā diligentiā et ardore exercentur,: calebant nundinae,: posteaquam satis calere res Rubrio visa est,i. e. seemed sufficiently ripe for execution,: Veneris bella calent,rage,: et mixtus lacrimis caluit dolor,.—
To be yet warm, new, or fresh (the figure taken from food): at enim nihil est, nisi, dum calet, hic agitur,: illi rumores de comitiis caluerunt, Cael. ap. .—
(Effectus pro causā.) Of a place, to be eagerly sought, to be frequented (rare): ungularum pulsibus calens Hister,often trod,.

callĕo, ēre, v. n. and a.
[callum].

Trop. *

la:noun:calumnia.gloss: A cunning device, trickery, artifice, sophistry, chicanery.
senses: A cunning device, trickery, artifice, sophistry, chicanery.
A misrepresentation, false statement, fallacy, cavil.
A false accusation or prosecution, malicious charge.
la:noun:calumnia.html:
călumnĭa (old form kălumnĭa;
v. the letter K), ae, f.
perh. for calvomnia, from calvor; cf. incīlo
, trickery, artifice, chicanery, cunning device.
Lit.
In gen.: per obtrectatores Lentuli calumniā extracta res est,: (Lucullus) inimicorum calumniā triennio tardius quam debuerat triumphavit,: inpediti ne triumpharent calumniā paucorum, quibus omnia honesta atque inhonesta vendere mos erat,: Metellus calumniā dicendi tempus exemit,: cum omni morā, ludificatione, calumniā senatūs auctoritas impediretur,.—Plur.: res ab adversariis nostris extracta est variis calumniis,.—
In partic.
A pretence, evasion, subterfuge: juris judicium cum erit et aequitatis, cave in istā tam frigidā, tam jejunā calumniā delitescas,: senatus religionis calumniam non religione, sed malevolentiā ... comprobat,: Carneades ... itaque premebat alio modo nec ullam adhibebat calumniam,: calumniam stultitiamque ejus obtrivit ac contudit,: illud in primis, ne qua calumnia, ne qua fraus, ne quis dolus adhibeatur,: quae major calumnia est, quam venire imberbum adulescentulum... dicere se filium senatorem sibi velle adoptare?.—
In discourse, etc., a misrepresentation, false statement, fallacy, cavil (cf.: cavillatio, perfugium): haec cum uberius disputantur et fusius, facilius effugiunt Academicorum calumniam,: (Carneades) saepe optimas causas ingenii calumniā ludificari solet,: nec Arcesilae calumnia conferenda est cum Democriti verecundiā,: si in minimis rebus pertinacia reprehenditur, calumnia etiam coërcetur,: altera est calumnia, nullam artem falsis adsentiri opinionibus,: si quis tamen... ad necessaria aliquid melius adjecerit, non erit hac calumniā reprendendus,.—
A false accusation, malicious charge, esp. a false or malicious information, or action at law, a perversion of justice ( = συκοφαντία): jam de deorum inmortalium templis spoliatis qualem calumniam ad pontifices adtulerit?false report,: Scythae ... cum confecto jam bello supervenissent, et calumniā tardius lati auxilii, mercede fraudarentur,an unjust charge,: quamquam illa fuit ad calumniam singulari consilio reperta ratio... Quae res cum ad pactiones iniquissimas magnam vim habuit, tum vero ad calumnias in quas omnes inciderent, quos vellent Apronius,: causam calumniae reperire,, § 21: (Heraclius), a quo HS. C. milia per calumniam malitiamque petita sunt,, § 66: mirari improbitatem calumniae,, § 37: exsistunt etiam saepe injuriae calumniā quādam et nimis callidā juris interpretatione,: iste amplam occasionem calumniae nactus,: quem iste in decumis, in rebus capitalibus, in omni calumniā praecursorem habere solebat et emissarium,, § 108; 2, 2, 9, § 25: ad rapinas convertit animum, vario et exquisitissimo calumniarum et auctionum et vectigalium genere,; cf. the context: calumniā litium alienos fundos petere,: adeo illis odium Romanorum incussit rapacitas proconsulum, sectio publicanorum, calumniae litium,: calumniarum metum inicere alicui,: principes confiscatos ob tam leve ac tam inpudens calumniarum genus, ut, etc.,: calumniis rapinisque intendit animum,: creditorum turbam... nonnisi terrore calumniarum amovit,: fiscales calumnias magna calumniantium repressit,—Plur.: istae calumniae,; cf.: calumnia magiae,, p. 274, 10.—
Hence, jurid. t. t., the bringing of an action, whether civil or criminal, in bad faith: actoris calumnia quoque coërcetur,litigiousness on the part of the plaintiff, Sandars ad loc.; Gai : vetus calumniae actio, a prosecution for blackmail or malicious prosecution, : calumniam jurare, to take the oath that the action is brought or defence offered in good faith, Cael. ap. : sei juraverit calumniae causā non postulare, Lex Acil. Repetund. 19; ; cf.: praeter jusjurandum exigere non calumniae causā infitias ire, Gai : jusjurandum exigere non calumniae causā agere,.—Hence: nec satis habere bello vicisse Hannibalem, nisi velut accusatores calumniam in eum jurarent ac nomen deferrent, Weissenb. ad loc; so, de calumniā jurare,: jusjurandum de calumniā, Gai ; : et quidem calumniae judicium adversus omnes actiones locum habet, a conviction in a cross-action for malicious prosecution, Gai : turpissimam personam calumniae honestae civitati inponere,to fasten the vile character of a malicious prosecutor upon,: sine ignominiā calumniae accusationem relinquere non posse,.— The person convicted of this charge was branded on the forehead with the letter K; v. calumniator.—
Transf., a conviction for malicious prosecution ( = calumniae judicium, v. I. A. 4. supra): hic illo privato judicio, mihi credite, calumniam non effugiet,: scito C. Sempronium Rufum, mel ac delicias tuas, calumniam maximo plausu tulisse, Cael. ap. : accusare alienae dominationis scelerisque socius propter calumniae metum non est ausus,: perinde poenā teneri ac si publico judicio calumniae condemnatus,: calumniam fictis eludere jocis,.—
Trop.
Of abstr. things: in hac igitur calumniā timoris et caecae suspitionis tormento, cum plurima ad alieni sensūs conjecturam, non ad suum judicium scribantur, i. e. when the writer's mind is made the fool of his fears, Caecil. ap. . —
Contra se, a mistaken severity towards one's self: inveni qui Ciceroni crederent, eum (Calvum) nimiā contra se calumniā verum sanguinem perdidisse, (referring to : nimium inquirens in se atque ipse sese observans, metuensque ne vitiosum colligeret, etiam verum sanguinem deperdebat).

To accuse falsely, bring false information against a person.
Absol.: calumniari est falsa crimina intendere,; cf. ib. prooem.: ut hic quoque Apronio... ex miseris aratoribus calumniandi quaestus accederet,: cum aliquid habeat quod possit criminose ac suspitiose dicere, aperte ludificari et calumniari sciens non videatur,: cum (defensor) accusatorem calumniari criminatur,: nondum Romam accusator Eumenes venerat, qui calumniando omnia detorquendoque suspecta et invisa efficeret,: tabulae veterum aerari debitorum, vel praecipua calumniandi materia,: magna calumniantium poena,: minus objectus calumniantibus foret,: calumniatur accusator actione sacrilegii, cum privata fuerit (pecunia sublata) non sacra,: an petitorem calumniari, an reum infitiatorem esse,.—
With acc.: si tamen alio crimine postuletur ab eodem, qui in alio crimine eum calumniatus est, puto non facile admittendum eum qui semel calumniatus est,: sed non utique qui non probat quod intendit calumniari videtur,.—
To practise chicanery, trickery, or subterfuge: jacet res in controversiis isto calumniante biennium,: meque, etiam si diutius calumniarentur. redire jussistis,.—
In gen., to depreciate, misrepresent, calumniate, to blame unjustly.

Esp., with se, to depreciate one's self, be unduly anxious or careful: quibusdam tamen nullus est finis calumniandi se, et... qui etiam, cum optima sunt reperta, quaerunt aliquid, quod sit magis antiquum, remotum, inopinatum,: neque eos... ad infelicem calumniandi se poenam alligandos puto,.—
Absol.: sed calumniabar ipse; putabam, qui obviam mihi venisset, suspicaturum,i. e. indulged unreasonable fears,; cf. A. 2. supra.—
With things as objects, to misrepresent, interpret injuriously, set in a false light: non calumniatur verba nec voltus; quicquid accidit, benigne interpretando levat,: suspitionibus inquietantur medicisque jam sani manum porrigunt et omnem calorem corporis sui calumniantur,: festinationem alicujus,: id unum,: jus civile,.
